meta_description: Company 1 business intelligence dashboard: a synthetic online food-delivery marketplace case study with 34 executive KPIs, unit economics, customers, operations, marketing efficiency, forecasting and optimization.
meta_font_stack: 'Instrument Sans', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Arial, sans-serif
hero_title: Company 1: growth, margin and the cost of every order
hero_sub: A synthetic online food-delivery marketplace, followed from single orders to a management decision on growth versus margin. Not affiliated with any real company; methodology is in the Sources section.
maker_role: Business Intelligence | Data Analytics | Data Engineering
sec_overview_desc: Latest month versus the previous month for 34 KPIs in seven groups. Each tile shows the value, the change, and a 12-month sparkline; green/red marks whether the move is good or bad for the business. Tiles tagged “3M” use a trailing 3-month window (sign-up-driven KPIs; see the Sources section). Hover a tile for its definition.
sec_financial_desc: Revenue, cost structure and what drives contribution margin. The headline contribution margin is shown before promotions; the after-promotion view charges the platform-funded discounts against it.
sec_unit_desc: What one delivered order earns and costs the platform — total, by cuisine, by restaurant tier and by payment method.
sec_customers_desc: Acquisition quality, retention, segments, subscription impact and how concentrated revenue is across the customer base.
sec_restaurants_desc: Which restaurants create profit, how concentrated volume is, and how supply keeps up with demand.
sec_operations_desc: Speed, reliability, cancellations, demand peaks, city-level performance and rider productivity.
sec_marketing_desc: Observed acquisition spend by channel, CAC versus assumptions, LTV:CAC and the real cost of promotions.
sec_forecast_desc: Twelve-month outlook with 80% intervals and the plan required to reach +25% orders and +2 pp contribution margin.
sec_optimization_desc: Downside / base / upside profit scenarios and the optimal allocation of a fixed promotion budget across city × segment cells.
sec_sources_desc: Everything on this page is computed from the synthetic dataset in this repository. No real company data is used.
def_gmv: Gross merchandise value of delivered orders (food + delivery fee + service fee) in the month.
def_gmv_yoy: GMV compared with the same month one year earlier.
def_delivered_orders: Orders with status Delivered or Refunded.
def_active_customers: Distinct customers with at least one delivered order in the month.
def_orders_per_active_customer: Delivered orders divided by active customers — order frequency.
def_platform_revenue: Commission + service fee + 35% of delivery fee, less the refund offset.
def_take_rate: Platform revenue as a share of GMV.
def_contribution_profit: Platform revenue − rider cost − payment processing − 50% of refunds. Headline definition: before promotions.
def_contribution_margin: Contribution profit as a share of platform revenue (before promotions).
def_contribution_per_order: Contribution profit divided by delivered orders.
def_revenue_per_order: Platform revenue divided by delivered orders.
def_cost_to_serve: Platform revenue − contribution profit, per delivered order (rider + payment + refund cost).
def_delivery_fee_coverage: Delivery fees collected as a share of rider cost — how much of delivery the customer pays for.
def_promotion_burden: Promotion cost (discounts funded by the platform) as a share of platform revenue.
def_new_customers: Customers who signed up in the month and ordered in it; average of the last 3 months.
def_new_share: New customers as a share of active customers; last 3 months pooled.
def_m1_retention: Of customers who signed up in the previous month, the share who ordered this month.
def_subscriber_share: Share of delivered orders placed by subscribed customers.
def_on_time_rate: Delivered orders arriving within 5 minutes of the estimate.
def_avg_delivery_minutes: Average actual delivery time of delivered orders.
def_very_late_rate: Delivered orders arriving more than 15 minutes late.
def_cancellation_rate: Cancelled orders as a share of all orders placed.
def_refund_rate: Refunded orders as a share of delivered orders.
def_avg_rating: Average customer rating (1–5) of delivered orders.
def_active_restaurants: Restaurants with at least one delivered order in the month.
def_orders_per_restaurant: Delivered orders divided by active restaurants.
def_active_riders: Riders who completed at least one order in the month.
def_rider_utilization: Busy hours as a share of online hours across all riders.
def_orders_per_rider_hour: Delivered orders divided by rider online hours.
def_marketing_spend: Observed acquisition spend across channels; monthly average of the last 3 months.
def_blended_cac: Marketing spend divided by sign-ups; last 3 months pooled.
def_marketing_pct_revenue: Marketing spend as a share of platform revenue; last 3 months pooled.
def_discount_rate: Discount amount as a share of GMV.
win_3m_title: Trailing 3-month window — sign-ups in the final month are truncated, so a single month would show a false drop.

ins_forecast: The selected model for delivered orders is {model}; the 12-month base case ends at {end} orders per month. Reaching +25% orders and +2 pp margin needs a combined plan, not a single lever.

c_gmv_orders: GMV and delivered orders by month
c_margin_promo: Contribution margin: before vs. after promotions
c_margin_promo_cap: The gap between the lines is the promotion cost, as a share of platform revenue.
c_drivers: Margin driver decomposition (first vs. last month)
c_rev_vs_cost: Revenue vs. cost to serve per order
c_segment_profit: Share of customers vs. share of profit
c_segment_profit_cap: Segments whose profit share exceeds their customer share are over-earning.
c_cohort: Cohort retention heatmap (% of sign-up cohort still ordering)
c_quadrant: Restaurant GMV vs. contribution margin (each dot = one restaurant)
c_supply: Supply: active restaurants and orders per restaurant
c_heatmap: Demand heatmap — orders by weekday × hour
c_heatmap_cap: Average delivered orders per day, last 3 months.
c_city_scorecard_cap: Green = better, red = worse within each column.
c_cac_compare: CAC: planning assumption vs. observed (last 3 months)
c_ltvcac_cap: Dashed line = break-even (1.0). A healthy channel is typically 3 or higher.
c_promo: Orders with vs. without a promotion
c_promo_cap: Contribution after promotions is the true per-order profit of a promoted order.
c_forecast: Delivered orders — history, forecast and 80% interval

src_data_v: Reproducible NumPy/pandas simulation (fixed seed) of ~12,000 customers, 320 restaurants, 520 riders and ~167k orders over 17 months, with seasonality, a growth trend, churn/retention curves and realistic financial relationships. v2 adds two tables: observed marketing spend by month × channel, and rider online/busy hours.
src_kpi_v: 34 scorecard KPIs computed from the order table in src/analytics/kpis.py. Delivered orders = Delivered + Refunded. Contribution profit is before promotions (the model’s headline definition); “after promotions” subtracts promotion cost. The scorecard compares the latest month with the previous month.
src_fc_v: Seasonal-naive, moving-average and Holt-Winters models compared via rolling-origin (temporal) validation; the best model is selected per metric by WAPE.
src_opt_v: SciPy trust-constr solves a concave-response promotion-budget allocation across city × segment cells, maximizing incremental contribution profit under a fixed budget.
src_seg_v: Rule-based on realized recency / frequency / monetary value and subscription status — not random labels.
src_def_v: Customer sign-ups are generated over a fixed window that ends on 2026-08-23, so the final month holds only part of its sign-ups. Sign-up-driven KPIs (new customers, new-customer share, marketing spend, CAC, marketing % of revenue) therefore use a trailing 3-month window, tagged “3M”.
src_lim_v: All data is synthetic: patterns such as retention, channel economics and city margins are model outputs, not market evidence. Per-order unit economics use the last 3 months; LTV is the observed lifetime profit to date, not a projection. Marketing spend and rider hours are generated tables too, with built-in CAC inflation for paid channels, so the gap between “observed” and planning CAC is a modelled outcome, not market evidence.

verdicts.Achievable, but only with a combined pla: Achievable, but only with a combined plan — no single lever gets there alone. The model shows the target requires simultaneous discount discipline, delivery-cost efficiency and a modest take-rate increase, not organic growth alone.
